cells.tense: Present tense — here, with the pen.
cells.verb: holding what the change produced, in a form that can be kept
cells.place: in pure pattern, where structure stands free of any single case
cells.ask: Offer one clear piece of what you've been holding to someone who can hand something back — exchange, not accounting; and let fairness move as it will, give and take in one flowing current, without tallying.
cells.core:
You've come through something and kept what it left. Not the story of it — the shape of it, the way it works, held steady enough to be passed on. That holding is a craft you're doing well right now.
And it's finished being only yours. What you preserved is ready to move between people — handed over, met with something in return, kept honest by the exchange. The form holds. Now let it circulate.
cells.sheetLine: You've preserved what the change made, and it's ready to move.

cells.tense: Future tense — bracing at a future that can't be written in.
cells.verb: holding what the change produced, grabbed tighter than the form needs
cells.place: in pure pattern, run ahead of anything that actually happened
cells.ask: Let the pattern sit as what it is and let one person actually feel it with you — recognition that keeps you and them both intact, close without merging. What comes back when this is in balance is a readiness that moves from what's genuinely felt, instead of from what might be.
cells.core:
You're guarding a shape from something that hasn't happened yet. The pattern keeps getting braced against a version you can see coming, and the holding has gone past preserving into gripping — the form is fine, it's the grip that's ahead of itself.
What the change left doesn't need defending from a future that isn't here. The endings already happened.
cells.sheetLine: You're defending a shape from a future that hasn't arrived.

cells.tense: Past tense — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: holding what the change produced, without picking the form back up
cells.place: in pure pattern, seen once and not kept
cells.ask: Gather your direction and defend it: pick one thing you actually want and move from the wanting, not from duty. What comes back when this is in balance is the change flowing again from felt necessity — endings honored, renewal trusted, because you're finally in motion on your own behalf.
cells.core:
The seeing happened, and the holding didn't. Somewhere back there the pattern was clear and you didn't take it up — no form, no keeping, the clarity left sitting where it landed.
So the change you came through has nowhere to stand. What's missing isn't more insight. It's the willingness to give what you saw a shape and keep it.
cells.sheetLine: You saw the pattern and never gave it a form to stand in.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: holding what the change produced, while calling the holding something the situation did
cells.place: in pure pattern, already steady and unnamed as yours
cells.ask: Take up the smaller, earlier form of this same thing: say plainly what you're keeping in place and why, and let it work as structure that serves rather than as a fact about the world. What comes back when this is in balance is the change running again from felt necessity, endings honored, renewal trusted — because the hand that built the form is finally visible.
cells.core:
You're already holding something steady — people around you organize against it, things settle because you've kept them from moving — and you talk about it like the situation did that itself.
The preserving is real and it's running. The claim on it isn't.
cells.sheetLine: You're already keeping it steady. You just haven't said it's you.
